question: Which of the following structural fragments, common in angiotensin II receptor antagonists, is ionized at physiological pH because it is acidic ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Tetrazole ring -> acidic at physiological pH -> ionized at physiological pH -> 95% CHAIN: Imidazole ring -> slightly acidic at physiological pH -> partially ionized at physiological pH -> 85% CHAIN: Hydroxyalkyl group -> not acidic at physiological pH -> not ionized at physiological pH -> 90% CHAIN: Biphenyl substructure -> not acidic at physiological pH -> not ionized at physiological pH -> 95%
analysis: The structural fragment that is acidic and ionized at physiological pH in angiotensin II receptor antagonists is the tetrazole ring.
